title: A Comprehensive Guide to Fractional Response Models with fracreg
text: fracreg package comprehensive tool available R estimating, diagnosing, interpreting fractional response models. supports: One-part models (1P): single process governs entire distribution y∈[0,1]y \[0, 1]. Two-part hurdle models (2P): Separately models binary hurdle (y>0y > 0) continuous fractional part (0<y≤10 < y \le 1). Three-part double-inflated models (3P): Handles inflation 0 1. Panel data models (fracregpd): CRE, QML, GMM approaches longitudinal data. Endogeneity correction (fracreghet): Control function IV-GMM approaches. vignette walks comprehensive empirical examples (using 401(k) dataset) simulated examples estimator.

title: A Comprehensive Guide to Fractional Response Models with fracreg

title: fracreg — Fractional Response Models
text: fracreg handles: Univariate Fractional Models (fracreg): Fit standard 1-part models, hurdle 2-part models (mass 0 1), double-inflated 3-part models. Panel Data Models (fracregpd): Estimate fractional models fixed-T longitudinal data, supporting Correlated Random Effects (CRE) handle unobserved individual heterogeneity. Endogeneity & Heteroscedasticity (fracreghet): Correct endogenous covariates using Instrumental Variables (IV) via Control Function GMM approaches. Diagnostic Testing: Includes generalised goodness--functional-form (fracreg.ggoff), RESET (fracreg.reset), non-nested P-tests (fracreg.ptest). Analytical Partial Effects: Compute exact marginal effects model types (including 3-part composite effects) via Delta method using fracreg.pe().

title: GGOFF Tests for Fractional Response Models — fracreg.ggoff
text: fracreg.ggoff applies GGOFF, GOFF1 GOOFF2 test statistics fractional response models estimated via fracreg. fracreg.ggoff may used test link specification : () one-part fractional response models; (ii) binary component two-part fractional response models; (iii) fractional component two-part fractional response models. GGOFF Test Framework: Generalised Goodness--Functional Form (GGOFF) test evaluates adequacy link function \(G(\cdot)\). based augmenting baseline model specific directions departure. auxiliary testing equation takes form: $$E(y|x) = G\left(x\beta + \gamma_1 \frac{g'(x\hat{\beta})}{g(x\hat{\beta})} + \gamma_2 x\hat{\beta} \right)$$ \(g(\cdot)\) \(g'(\cdot)\) first second derivatives \(G(\cdot)\) evaluated linear predictor \(x\hat{\beta}\). test checks \(H_0: \gamma_1 = 0, \gamma_2 = 0\). GOFF1 GOFF2 variants testing individual components. Wald version implemented, taken account option chosen computing standard errors model evaluation. LM version, robust version computed cases () (iii) conventional version case (ii). See Ramalho, Ramalho Murteira (2014) details application GGOFF, GOFF1 GOOFF2 tests fractional response framework.

title: Fitting Fractional Response Models — fracreg
text: fracreg estimates one-part, two-part hurdle, three-part double-inflated fractional response models; see Ramalho, Ramalho Murteira (2011) Fang Ma (2013) details models. One-Part Fractional Response Models (type = "1P"): standard one-part model assumes conditional expectation fractional response \(y_i \[0,1]\) given : $$E(y_i|x_i) = G(x_i \beta)$$ \(G(\cdot)\) known non-linear link function mapping linear predictor unit interval (e.g., logit, probit). parameters \(\beta\) estimated maximising Bernoulli-based quasi-log-likelihood function: $$\ln L_i(\beta) = y_i \ln[G(x_i \beta)] + (1 - y_i) \ln[1 - G(x_i \beta)]$$ estimator requires correct specification conditional mean yield consistent parameter estimates (Papke Wooldridge, 1996). Two-Part Hurdle Models (type = "2P"): data exhibits boundary mass (e.g., \(y_i = 0\)), two-part hurdle model handles boundary values separately interior fractional values. Let \(y_i^*\) binary indicator \(y_i^* = 1\) \(y_i > 0\) \(y_i^* = 0\) otherwise. probability observing boundary value modelled : $$P(y_i = 0 | x_{1i}) = 1 - F(x_{1i} \gamma_1)$$ $$P(y_i > 0 | x_{1i}) = F(x_{1i} \gamma_1)$$ \(F(\cdot)\) binary link function. Conditional observing interior fractional value, response modelled : $$E(y_i | x_{2i}, y_i > 0) = G(x_{2i} \beta_2)$$ unconditional mean response therefore: $$E(y_i|x_i) = F(x_{1i} \gamma_1) \times G(x_{2i} \beta_2)$$ Three-Part Double Inflated Models (type = "3P"): data containing boundary mass \(0\) \(1\), three-part model estimates two separate binary mechanisms boundary fractional component interior values \((0, 1)\), extending two-part logic double inflation (Fang Ma, 2013). fracreg uses standard glm command perform estimations. Therefore, fracreg essentially convenience command, allowing estimation several alternative fractional response models using command. addition, fracreg provides R-squared measure models (calculated square correlation coefficient actual fitted values dependent variable), calculates fitted values dependent variable two-part models stores information needed implement useful commands fractional response models: fracreg.reset (RESET test), fracreg.ptest (P test), fracreg.ggoff (GGOFF tests) fracreg.pe (partial effects).

text: fracreg.pe calculates partial effects fractional response models estimated via fracreg. fracreg.pe may used compute average conditional partial effects : () one-part fractional response models; (ii) binary components two-part three-part fractional response models; (iii) fractional components two-part three-part fractional response models; (iv) two-part three-part fractional response models overall. Partial Effects Continuous Variables: continuous covariate \(x_k\), partial effect conditional mean \(E(y|x) = G(x\beta)\) first derivative respect \(x_k\): $$PE_k(x) = \frac{\partial E(y|x)}{\partial x_k} = g(x\beta)\beta_k$$ \(g(\cdot)\) probability density function corresponding link function \(G(\cdot)\). Partial Effects Discrete Variables: discrete dummy covariate \(x_k\), partial effect calculated discrete difference expected value \(x_k\) changes 0 1, holding variables \(x_{-k}\) constant: $$PE_k(x) = G(x_{-k}\beta_{-k} + \beta_k) - G(x_{-k}\beta_{-k})$$ Average vs. Conditional Partial Effects: - Average Partial Effects (APE): Evaluated observation \(\) sample averaged: $$APE_k = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{=1}^N PE_k(x_i)$$ - Conditional Partial Effects (CPE): Evaluated specific vector covariate values \(x^*\) (e.g., sample mean median): $$CPE_k = PE_k(x^*)$$ calculating standard errors, taken account option previously chosen estimating model. code: ### Empirical 401(k) Examples  data("fracreg_k401k")  y <- fracreg_k401k$prate  X_het <- cbind(mrate = fracreg_k401k$mrate, age = fracreg_k401k$age)   # fracreghet estimators do not allow exact 1s or 0s y_adj <- y y_adj[y_adj == 1] <- 0.999  # Artificial instrumental variable for demonstration  set.seed(42) Z_emp <- cbind(X_het, z = fracreg_k401k$mrate * rnorm(length(y)))  res_emp <- fracreghet(y_adj, X_het, type="GMMx", link="logit", table=FALSE)  fracreghet.reset(res_emp) #> Warning: step size truncated due to divergence #> RESET test could not be computed; either algorithm did not converge (Wald version) or covariance matrix is singular (Wald/LM versions)   ### Simulated Examples  N <- 250 u <- rnorm(N)  X <- cbind(rnorm(N),rnorm(N)) dimnames(X)[[2]] <- c("X1","X2")  Z <- cbind(rnorm(N),rnorm(N),rnorm(N)) dimnames(Z)[[2]] <- c("Z1","Z2","Z3")  y <- exp(X[,1]+X[,2]+u)/(1+exp(X[,1]+X[,2]+u))  res <- fracreghet(y,X,type="GMMx",table=FALSE)  #LM and Wald versions of the RESET test, based on 1 or 2 fitted powers of xb fracreghet.reset(res,2:3,c("Wald","LM")) #>  #> --------------------------------------------------------------------------------  #>                                    RESET test  #> --------------------------------------------------------------------------------  #>                        Fractional logit regression model  #> --------------------------------------------------------------------------------  #> H0: Estimator: GMMx  #> --------------------------------------------------------------------------------  #>         Statistic p-value #> LM(2)       0.584   0.445 #> Wald(2)     0.552   0.458 #> LM(3)       0.809   0.667 #> Wald(3)     0.686   0.710 #> --------------------------------------------------------------------------------  #>                          Run Date: 2026-07-06 01:18:20  #> --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

title: Fitting Panel Data Fractional Response Models — fracregpd
text: fracregpd computes GMM estimators proposed Ramalho, Ramalho Coelho (2018) panel data fractional response models time-variant time-invariant unobserved heterogeneity endogeneous covariates: GMMww, GMMc, GMMbgw, GMMpfe, GMMcre GMMpre. addition, fracregpd also computes QMLcre, proposed Papke Wooldridge (2008) Wooldridge (2019). Correlated Random Effects (CRE) - QMLcre: panel data, unobserved individual-specific heterogeneity \(c_i\) may correlated covariates \(x_{}\). CRE approach (Papke Wooldridge, 2008) models dependence projecting \(c_i\) onto time averages strictly exogenous covariates \(\bar{x}_i\): $$c_i = \psi + \bar{x}_i \xi + a_i$$ \(a_i\) error term independent \(x_i\). Assuming \(a_i | x_i \sim N(0, \sigma_a^2)\) probit link, integrating \(a_i\) yields "population-averaged" scaled conditional mean: $$E(y_{} | x_i) = G(x_{} \beta_a + \psi_a + \bar{x}_i \xi_a)$$ parameters subscript \(\) scaled \((1 + \sigma_a^2)^{-1/2}\). equation estimated via pooled Bernoulli QML. Generalised Method Moments (GMM): models strict exogeneity fails link function exponential-type link, Ramalho et al. (2018) propose GMM estimators based following general moment conditions: $$E[Z_{} (H(y_{}) - \exp(x_{}\beta + c_i))] = 0$$ \(H(\cdot)\) transformation function \(Z_{}\) matrix valid instruments. Estimators GMMww, GMMc, GMMbgw use different transformations eliminate unobserved fixed effect \(c_i\) applying GMM. overidentified models, fracregpd calculates Hansen's J statistic test validity overidentifying restrictions.
